findings.issue: The narrative introduction, “And I replied,” is omitted. The draft begins directly with the contents of the reply, whereas the supplied Greek explicitly identifies the speaker and the act of answering.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore “And I replied,” before “I now pass over,” and mark the ensuing speech consistently with the preceding passage. The amended passage requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἥτις ἐὰν ἐπιθυμίαν (Πολυξένην) ὡς ἀληθείας ἀλλοτρίαν οὖσαν καὶ ξένην ἐπιθυμῇ
findings.english_quote: If that prime desires Desire—Polyxena—who is alien and foreign to truth
findings.issue: The relative clause gives a defensible characterization of Desire, but the treatment of ὡς with οὖσαν is not explained. The construction can characterize her “as being” alien to truth or present that characterization as the represented reason for desiring her. The draft's notes do not disclose this distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note explaining that the main text takes the phrase descriptively, while “as being alien and foreign to truth” or a causal reading, “because she is alien and foreign to truth,” remains possible. Alternatively, consider retaining “as being” explicitly in the main text. Review the resulting wording and note afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἰῷ ὄφεως ἀναιρεῖται βέλει κατὰ πτέρναν καὶ κατὰ ἴχνος ἐνέρποντος τοῦ θανάτου.
findings.english_quote: it is killed by a serpent’s venom in an arrow to the heel, as death creeps in along the footprint.
findings.issue: The note discloses alternatives for the two instrumental datives, but not the materially different senses of ἴχνος or the attachment of the coordinated κατὰ phrases. “Footprint” selects a track image; ἴχνος can also denote the sole or foot. Both κατὰ πτέρναν and κατὰ ἴχνος can be understood with death's creeping entrance, rather than assigning the first exclusively to the arrow. These are interpretive uncertainties, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Extend the note to explain that the main text attaches “at the heel” to the arrow and reads ἴχνος as a footprint or track. Preserve the alternative in which death creeps in at the heel and at the sole of the foot. Reassess the main wording against those alternatives without filling or changing the supplied Greek.

findings.source_quote: ἐπ’ ὀλέθρῳ ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ τῶν αὐτοῦ
findings.english_quote: τῶν αὐτοῦ is deliberately broad and may denote his people, household, or possessions; “those who are his” preserves that ambiguity.
findings.issue: The personal main-text rendering is defensible, and the note already names the possessions alternative. However, its claim that “those who are his” preserves the entire ambiguity is inaccurate: “who” selects persons rather than possessions. The distinction between the main-text choice and the alternative therefore needs more honest description.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the note to state that the main text selects his people or household in the Paris allegory, while the Greek can also refer to his possessions. Alternatively, consider “both himself and his own” as a broader main-text candidate. Any amended wording or rationale requires fresh review; the referent ambiguity itself does not require blocking.
